summary.headline: Shree Refrigerations FY26 revenue rose about 50% to INR153 crore and PAT to INR21 crore, with H2 EBITDA margin at 26.3% against 11% in H1.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR153 crore (roughly 50%+ growth), PAT up about 64% and reported EPS up 28% to INR6.47 despite the IPO dilution. H2 revenue of about INR100 crore was roughly double H1's INR50 crore, as H1 was spent on design and type-test approvals, machine additions and a new Wajeri facility. Working capital days fell from 570 to 370, and the closing order book was INR270 crore. Management guided to 20-24% EBITDA margin going forward and 40% revenue CAGR for 3-5 years, with data centre revenue expected only from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Up about 50%+ YoY (management cited ~150% growth in one place; call transcript inconsistent)
Up about 100% YoY and HoH vs INR50 crore in H1
Up from INR13 crore; PAT up about 64% YoY per management
Up 28% YoY from INR5 despite higher share count
from INR118 crore, on IPO and profit
from 570 days; receivable days 350 to 250; inventory days 250 to 230

segments.name: Defence / naval HVAC, AC plant and refrigeration
segments.commentary: Core business with management-stated 64%-plus market share; 8 ongoing projects, 4 of which are expected to complete in FY27. Order book INR270 crore at March-end, mostly HVAC, AC plant and refrigeration.

segments.name: Spares, service and AMC
segments.commentary: Fell to about 7% of revenue in FY26 from about 30% last year; management targets 15% (and 15-20% in another answer) to lift EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Data centre cooling (via Smardt tie-up)
segments.commentary: Channel partnership about six months old; reference installation targeted in FY27, with major revenue expected from FY28. No data centre revenue assumed in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected at 20-24% going forward; management said commodity inflation was considered in this guidance.
Growth guided at about 40% CAGR for 3-5 years; CEO reiterated INR1,000 crore revenue target within about 5 years and INR120-130 crore PAT target for FY30-31 from the earlier presentation.
FY27 guidance excludes data centre revenue.
FY27 order inflow expected to be lumpier across halves but H2 still expected to be bigger than H1; management says the skew will be reduced.
Working capital days expected to keep improving from 370 days; GST input credit refund expected to reduce other current assets in H1 FY27.
Management said the business needs no major capex for at least a couple of years; growth to be funded by internal accruals and bank working capital funding.
capex_capacity: Hanbarwadi Phase 1 capex INR25 crore, mostly spent; plant to start commercial production in June 2026.
Leased unit (about 20,000 sq ft) to close in June 2026; owned facility brings manufacturing space to about 70,000-80,000 sq ft, expandable by a further 50,000 sq ft.
Management says existing infrastructure can generate up to about INR400 crore of revenue at peak.
New Kochi office planned in FY27; new ATU controlled-ambient test room and AC plant and wet plant test facilities added.
Six AC plant capacities standardised by Navy: four type-tested; all six ATU and all AFU capacities type-tested; about 70% of ventilation fan variants type-tested.
demand_pricing: Navy plans to grow from about 150 ships to about 230 over 5-7 years; AONs of INR2.3-2.4 lakh crore granted, translating into orders over two years.

Management estimates its addressable share at about 1% of project cost, i.e. about INR2,500 crore defence TAM over two years, plus about INR500 crore non-defence; total TAM stated at INR3,000-3,500 crore over about 2-2.5 years.
Retrofit hit rate close to 100%; newbuild tenders lost in some cases.
Expected defence tenders of about INR1,000 crore to be floated in FY27; win rate not guided.
Data centre cooling is about 12-13% of data centre project value; data centre cooling market stated at USD 2.99 billion growing to about USD 9 billion over 3 years (25-30% CAGR).
Commodity inflation (copper and other metals) acknowledged; fixed-price projects of 2-3 years carry risk, with impact called small versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 H1/H2 revenue phasing and why was FY26 skewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be less skewed than FY26 but H2 will still be bigger; shipyard delivery schedules drive timing, and more concurrent projects should smooth it.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin range should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Kothale guided 20-24% EBITDA margin going forward, and management said commodity inflation was factored into this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre revenue timing and is it in the 40% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Reference installation in FY27 and major data centre revenue from FY28; FY27 guidance excludes data centre revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR1,000 crore revenue target reconcile with 40% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40% growth would reach about INR833 crore, but it stands by INR1,000 crore within about 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will external fundraising be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: No; working capital growth to be funded through internal accruals and bank funding, with a non-leveraged balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Export plans are nascent and limited to marine (defence/naval) business, not data centre; no details given.

qa_highlights.question: Danfoss servicing tie-up size?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed Turbocor Authorized Service Partner; revenue not significant at present as the installed base is about 1,200-1,300 compressors, described as a strategic capability step.

risks_watch: Revenue skew to H2 and lumpy delivery timing by shipyards; quarterly reporting declined by management.
Metal and commodity inflation on fixed-price projects of 2-3 years; margin guidance depends on it.
Spares and service share (7% in FY26) must recover to 15%+ to support margin.
Working capital still 370 days; GST input credit refund (other current assets up 6x to INR19.94 crore) pending.
Data centre revenue depends on Smardt product qualification; competition from around 30-40 global players, with most already present in India.
Management says main-board listing not allowed for about two more years.
Some newbuild tenders lost; FY27 defence tender flow of about INR1,000 crore is an uncertainty on order inflow.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term story (40% CAGR, INR1,000 crore target, data centre), while being evasive on quarterly reporting and on specifics such as data centre revenue sizing and export plans. Management repeatedly stated that the FY26 H1/H2 skew came from project and delivery timing.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that we will achieve the guidance that has been given by our CEO.
INR1,000 crore is the ladder which we are here in next 5 years and it will happen, sir.
Data centre revenue will start trickling in from next year onward, FY28 and onward, not in FY27.
So, for next going forward, we expect that our EBITDA margin will remain somewhere between 20% to 24%.
